Definition_of_value_1: The frame includes events in which two or more competitors share a single result.
The frame includes events contested by single competitors.
Opponents compete at the same time in the same space and can directly affect each other's performance.
The result depends on officials' assessment of execution, difficulty or style.
The result is settled by time, distance, weight or an equivalent objective measurement.
Deliberate bodily contact with an opponent is a normal part of play.
Play uses a ball.
A bat, racket, club, stick, bow, blade, rifle, oar, pole or ski pole is held and used.
A net or goal acts as a target or as a divider between sides.
Competitors ride a bike, boat, board, sled, pair of skis or pair of skates.
A helmet, mask or comparable head protection is standard competition equipment.
An animal takes part in the competition.
Normally contested on natural grass or an equivalent turf surface.
The standard competition venue is indoors.
Contested on ice or snow.
Contested in or on water.
Normally contested in the open air.
Contested inside a pitch, court, rink, ring, arena or lane of standardised dimensions.

Accuracy at a target, gate or hole is a central skill.
Sustained running is a main activity.
Jumping or aerial elements are a major scored or tactical component.
